findings.message: `resolve_for_read` handles an explicit track ID locally and returns before constructing `TrackResolutionInput` or calling the wired driver. This reimplements the READ explicit-override resolution rule in the bin, contrary to the thin-bin policy and the briefing requirement that ADR-baseline resolution flow through `track_resolution_driver()`. Pass the optional ID through `ReadFromItems` and let the driver/usecase resolve it.

`TrackItemsDirectoryInput::try_new` rejects paths containing `..`, whereas the replaced `track_resolve_project_root` accepted canonical-suffix paths such as `../track/items`. Invoking ADR-baseline from a repository subdirectory now fails with exit 1 instead of operating on the repository, violating CN-01/AC-05 compatibility. Preserve or normalize previously valid paths at the compatibility boundary.

`normalize_items_dir!` implements path normalization, branching, and a current-directory lookup inside the bin. This is application-level transformation and orchestration, contrary to the thin-bin requirement that `apps/cli` only construct typed inputs, obtain a wired driver, and emit its outcome. Move compatibility handling into the track-resolution driver/usecase/adapter boundary.

Lexically resolving `..` with `PathBuf::pop()` can retarget persistence. For example, if `/repo-a/link` points to `/repo-b/subdir`, the legacy path `/repo-a/link/../track/items` resolves through the filesystem to `/repo-b/track/items`, while this macro rewrites it to `/repo-a/track/items`. Snapshot or restore can consequently operate on the wrong repository. Preserve filesystem path semantics rather than lexically collapsing parent components.

`normalize_items_dir!` performs branching path-resolution logic and direct filesystem I/O (`std::fs::canonicalize`) in the bin. This violates the thin-bin policy and the briefing’s explicit instruction not to reintroduce `normalize_items_dir`; compatibility validation belongs in `TrackItemsDirectoryInput` or the resolution adapter.

Canonicalizing before validating changes the accepted CLI contract. For example, an existing `track/tmp/../items` path was rejected by the legacy helper because it was not lexically `<project-root>/track/items`, but canonicalization rewrites it to that directory and allows snapshot/restore to proceed. It also rewrites paths shown in failure diagnostics. This changes arguments, stderr, exit behavior, and potentially persistence contrary to CN-01.

`track_next_task_resolved` now requires `items_dir` to end in `<project-root>/track/items` and invokes `git rev-parse` through `build_branch_reader`; the same regression exists in `track_task_counts_resolved`. These pre-resolved paths previously queried `FsTrackStore` directly, and the CLI accepts other items-root paths when an explicit track ID is supplied. T001 therefore changes existing command behavior and adds unnecessary direct I/O even though the legacy query API never reads the injected branch reader. Keep this wiring off the legacy resolved paths until the lifecycle driver owns active selection.

The five lifecycle ports added to `TrackServiceImpl` are only retained in underscore-prefixed fields; no `TrackService` method consumes them, and every method still enters the old `TrackCompositionRoot` execution path. Consequently every `track_driver()` constructs unused adapters and `Arc` references, while future command interactors cannot receive them through the erased `Arc<dyn TrackService>`. This is dead runtime wiring in the compatibility facade rather than a usable DI handoff and obstructs the T002 migration seam.

`ReviewCompositionRoot::review_run_codex` and the other review entry points reach this helper, which calls `TrackResolutionDriver::resolve`; that method executes `TrackResolutionService::execute`. This leaves application-flow invocation inside `cli_composition`. The CLI caller should obtain the wired driver from `TrackCompositionRoot` and invoke it outside the composition layer.

The migrated helper constructs user-facing diagnostics (`invalid --track-id` here and `current workspace has no active track` below) and translates `TrackResolutionOutcome` into command-facing errors. Diagnostic rendering/mapping belongs in `cli_driver` or the CLI boundary; `cli_composition` should only wire and return the driver.

`TrackResolutionDriver::resolve` is a public primary-adapter operation but returns `TrackResolutionOutcome` instead of `CommandOutcome`. This leaves error rendering and exit-code signaling to callers, contrary to the cli_driver boundary contract; map failures to `CommandOutcome.stderr` and return the rendered outcome from the driver.

`TrackResolutionDriver::resolve` is a public primary-adapter operation but returns `TrackResolutionOutcome` instead of `CommandOutcome`. Errors therefore remain unrendered and exit-code signaling is delegated to callers, violating the cli_driver boundary contract.
T002–T013 descriptions name command groups but no target file or symbol, so an executor must invent the implementation boundary. T014 similarly omits the concrete resolution call-site files.

T002–T014 bundle independently verifiable command-context units (for example T002 init/archive and T004 add-task/next-task/transition) into single tasks without naming separate boundaries; propose task splits before implementation.

AC-06 and AC-07 are mapped only to T015, but T015 describes integration regressions and does not include a catalogue-lint validation step, canonical review-results check, or `cargo make ci-track` validation. These acceptance criteria therefore lack a plausible completing task.

T001 removes the composition root’s public execution methods (`no public execution methods`) but does not update the existing CLI callers; those updates begin in T002–T027. Therefore batch B1 cannot remain CI-green as required by CN-02. Move the caller migration into T001 or make the command tasks precede/remain part of the same compiling batch.

T001 adds the contract-like prose “with shared typed inputs while preserving the existing caller-facing execution-method surface.” This restates upstream type/behavior requirements instead of limiting the task text to target + operation + anchor cite.

T029 adds the outcome requirement “recording only a zero-findings, CI-green completion,” which restates AC-07 in the task description. Keep the validation commands and anchor, but remove the duplicated acceptance-contract prose.

T001 is attributed final ownership of `TrackCompositionRoot` and `TrackDriver`, but their catalogue shapes reference services/drivers introduced only by T002–T027 (`TrackInitService`…`TrackViewsValidateService`, `TrackTdddDriver`, and `TrackResolutionDriver`). Because T001 runs first and every migration task depends on it, these entries cannot conform at T001 completion while remaining CI-green. Move convergence ownership to a post-migration task such as T028, or restructure the task order and boundaries.

T023 owns the aggregate `TrackTdddDriver` and `TrackTdddInput`, but its lint-only task precedes T024–T026. Those catalogue shapes require the ContractMap, SpecElementHash, and TypeGraph inputs/services owned by those later tasks, so they cannot converge when T023 completes without implementing undocumented future-task work. Attribute the aggregates after T026 or reorder/rescope the tasks.

T027's attributed usecase entries declare module `track_lifecycle::resolution_compat`, its primary adapter declares `cli_driver::track_resolution`, and it owns an infrastructure adapter, but the task instead targets `libs/usecase/src/track_resolution.rs` and `apps/cli-composition/src/track/resolution.rs` without naming the required usecase, CLI-driver, or infrastructure targets. The described implementation therefore cannot converge with its attributed catalogue entries; align the task targets and operations with those declared modules.

T027 bundles four independently verifiable units: establishing the resolution boundary/wiring (IN-04/AC-04) and separately migrating the ADR-baseline, review-v2, and task-contract consumers (each IN-04/CN-01/AC-05). Each consumer has a distinct write target and focused regression surface while the old helpers can remain until T028. Split the foundation and consumer migrations into independently committable tasks before implementation starts.

Sections S1–S4 restate upstream sequencing and behavior in prose (for example, “before any caller migration”, “independently through…”, and “after their driver is wired”) instead of limiting themselves to concrete targets, operations, and anchor citations. Replace these restatements with target/operation/cite descriptions as required by `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

T027 still bundles independently verifiable units: establish the resolution boundary/wiring and migrate the ADR-baseline, review-v2, and task-contract consumers. Each consumer has a distinct write target and its own AC-05 regression surface while the legacy helpers can remain until T028. Split this into a foundation-plus-first-consumer task and separate review-v2 and task-contract migration tasks; each should cover IN-04/CN-01/AC-05, with T028 depending on all of them.

`plan.summary` says `GO-01 → T001–T029`, but the current plan also contains T030 and T031, which implement two IN-04 resolution-consumer migrations. Goal-to-task traceability therefore omits these tasks; update the summary to include them.

T028 includes final convergence/removal work explicitly anchored to OUT-03 and OUT-04, although the briefing marks semantic_dup/final convergence/crate reorganization as out of scope. Remove that work from this task or constrain it to the in-scope migration.

T001 restates an upstream architecture contract in prose: “proving `TaskQueryInteractor` remains co-located in the command-context module and is not split into another crate.” Keep the target, operation, and anchor cite, but remove this behavioral/rationale restatement per `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

T029 cannot successfully run `bin/sotp review check-approved` as an implementation step. Entering the task changes `impl-plan.json` to `in_progress`, and the batch later changes it to `done`, so the impl-plan review hash is stale until the workflow's post-implementation review. Moving T029 to B20 does not resolve this ordering problem because review still occurs after task implementation. Remove this check from the task and rely on the review/commit workflow, or otherwise move it to a post-review workflow stage.

T028 is still `todo` but bundles several independently verifiable behavior units: final composition-root/driver reference convergence (AC-01/AC-04), branch-strategy and selection port/adapter migrations (AC-03/CN-01), and metadata port/adapter migration with persistence regression (AC-03/AC-05). Split these units before implementation and redistribute their task-contract attributions and estimates; each can be completed and tested at its own call sites without requiring the other units.

T029 cannot successfully run `bin/sotp review check-approved` during implementation: its own `todo → in_progress → done` transitions change `impl-plan.json`, leaving the impl-plan review hash stale until the subsequent review phase. B20 therefore still invokes approval before the required approval artifact exists. Remove this check from the implementation task and leave it to the review/commit workflow, or move it to a genuine post-review stage.

T028 is `todo` but bundles independently verifiable units: composition-root/driver reference convergence (AC-01/AC-04), branch-strategy and selection port/adapter migrations (AC-03/CN-01), and metadata port/adapter migration with persistence regression (AC-03/AC-05). Split these units before implementation and redistribute their task-contract attributions and estimates.

B20 avoidably serializes T029 after T028. Once T028 is placed first in B19, T029's sole dependency is satisfied; T029 has no write target and declares zero lines, so adding it to B19 leaves totals at usecase 300, infrastructure 250, cli_driver 310, cli_composition 380, and cli 480—each within the 500-line ceiling. Put T029 after T028 in B19 and remove B20.

T028 is `todo` but bundles independently verifiable units: composition-root/driver reference convergence (AC-01/AC-04), branch-strategy and selection port/adapter migrations (AC-03/CN-01), and metadata port/adapter migration with persistence regression (AC-03/AC-05). Split these units before implementation and redistribute their task-contract attributions and estimates.

The `plan.summary` GO-01 traceability is stale: it says `GO-01 → T001–T031`, but the plan now includes T032 and T033 as additional implementation tasks. Update the summary so goal-to-task traceability covers the complete task set.

Section S4 includes T032 and T033, but its description only identifies resolution compatibility and three consumer contexts; it does not identify the branch-strategy/selection or metadata-port migrations those tasks perform. Add those targets and operations to S4 or move the tasks to an accurately described section.

Batch B2 groups T027 and T033 despite a concrete write-target collision in `libs/usecase/src/track_lifecycle/mod.rs`: T027 must register the new `track_lifecycle::resolution_compat` module there, while T033 targets `TrackMetadataPort`, which is declared in that same file, and budgets usecase production/test edits. These independent tasks therefore lack isolated write ownership and cannot safely share B2; move T033 to a non-overlapping batch or assign the shared file to one task.

T010 and T032 are both todo and become ready after T001, but T032 is deferred to B19 while B11 remains a singleton containing T010. Their declared targets do not overlap: T010 owns `track_set_override.rs` and its CLI/driver/composition wiring, while T032 owns `TrackBranchStrategyPort`/`TrackSelectionPort` and the corresponding infrastructure adapters. Their combined estimates are usecase 430, infrastructure 240, cli_driver 95, cli_composition 105, and cli 130—each below the 500-line ceiling. Move T032 into B11 alongside T010; T028 can continue to depend on it from B19.

B2 groups T027 and T033 despite a concrete write-ownership collision in `libs/usecase/src/track_lifecycle/mod.rs`: `resolution_compat.rs` does not yet exist, so T027 must register/re-export its new `TrackResolution*` module from that parent file, while T033 targets `TrackMetadataPort`, which is declared in the same file. Move T033 to B18 with T026; those targets do not overlap and their combined estimates remain within every 500-line ceiling (usecase 420, infrastructure 310, cli_driver 230, cli_composition 220, cli 240).

T014 and T033 are both todo and ready immediately after T001, but T033 is deferred to B18 while B15 remains a singleton containing T014. Their declared write targets do not overlap: T014 owns `track_task_counts.rs` and its CLI/driver/composition path, while T033 owns `TrackMetadataPort` and `FsTrackMetadataAdapter` in the usecase/infrastructure layers. Their combined estimates are usecase 315, infrastructure 160, cli_driver 85, cli_composition 95, and cli 120, all below the 500-line ceiling. Move T033 into B15 alongside T014; T026 can remain in B18.

T032 is still `todo` but bundles two independently verifiable behavior units: (1) migrating `TrackBranchStrategyPort` with `FsTrackBranchStrategyAdapter`, and (2) migrating `TrackSelectionPort` with `GitTrackSelectionAdapter`. Each has its own adapter-contract regression and can independently verify AC-03/CN-01. Split them into separate ordered tasks before implementation begins.

The adapter exposes environment-dependent absolute paths through the usecase-facing `DiagnosticText`: canonicalization failures include `git.root().display()`, missing-track errors include `track_dir.display()`, and `FsCommitHashStore` errors are forwarded verbatim. These diagnostics can reach CLI stderr and disclose the local repository layout. Return stable, path-free diagnostics (or sanitize paths) at this boundary.

Production errors from this adapter expose environment-dependent absolute paths through the usecase-facing `DiagnosticText`: canonicalization failures include `git.root().display()`, missing-track errors include `track_dir.display()`, and `FsCommitHashStore` errors are forwarded verbatim. These diagnostics can reach CLI stderr and disclose the local repository layout; sanitize paths or return stable path-free diagnostics at this boundary.

The new error mappers sanitize paths by discarding nearly all underlying diagnostics: `TrackReadError::Repository::Message`, `TrackWriteError::Repository::Message`, Git command failures (including stderr), render I/O errors, and commit-hash I/O errors all become generic text. This loses actionable distinctions such as malformed metadata, permission failures, symlink rejection, and Git stderr, violating the adapter contract to preserve diagnostic information. Preserve safe error details while removing only environment-dependent paths.
Re-reading the current briefing, severity policy, scoped file, and diff before the final re-adjudication.

The adapter still collapses important underlying failures into generic diagnostics: HEAD-resolution errors are discarded at `map_err(|_| ...)`, `CommitHashError::Io` loses its safe error kind/detail, and active-track resolution loses the specific detached/non-track/invalid-branch reason. This violates the briefing’s requirement to preserve diagnostic information while avoiding absolute paths; retain safe structured reasons rather than discarding them.

`TrackSelection::Explicit` is returned without the existing write guard. The current views-sync path verifies that an explicit ID matches the branch-derived track before rendering; this adapter would let `FsTrackViewsAdapter::sync` overwrite another track's rendered files from the wrong branch. Resolve explicit view selections through the write-guarded branch comparison and add a mismatch regression test.

`TrackSelection::Active` propagates branch discovery/resolution failures, so views sync on `main`, detached HEAD, or outside Git cannot select `RegistryOnly`. The existing command deliberately falls back to registry-only synchronization when no active track is detected; this changes its exit/output behavior and leaves the adapter's `RegistryOnly` path unreachable. Preserve that fallback and test a non-track branch.

The only `GitTrackCommitHashAdapter` test exits at the branch-mismatch check, before HEAD resolution, trusted-root handling, or `.commit_hash` persistence. It therefore cannot fulfill the bound `persist_current_for_track` contract or the required happy-path coverage. Add an adapter-level success test that verifies the returned HEAD and persisted file, plus the relevant I/O failure path.

`TrackSelection::Explicit` bypasses the existing views-sync write guard and returns the requested track without verifying that the current branch is `track/<id>`. Once this adapter is wired, `FsTrackViewsAdapter::sync` can overwrite another track's rendered files from the wrong branch. Resolve explicit view selections through the branch-matching write guard and test mismatch rejection before synchronization.

The active view-selection path propagates branch discovery/resolution failures instead of returning `RegistryOnly`. Existing views-sync behavior intentionally falls back to registry-only synchronization on `main`, detached HEAD, or Git discovery failure; the new implementation changes that behavior and never produces `RegistryOnly` itself. Preserve the fallback and cover a non-track branch.

`Path::is_dir()` silently converts every metadata error—including permission failures—into `false`, which is then misreported as a missing track. This loses required adapter diagnostics and also follows directory symlinks during the precheck. Use fallible `symlink_metadata`/`metadata`, distinguish `NotFound`, reject symlinks explicitly, and propagate other I/O failures through `DiagnosticText`.

The only adapter-level test for `persist_current_for_track` exits at the branch-mismatch check, before HEAD resolution, trusted-root validation, or `.commit_hash` persistence, yet it is recorded as fulfilling the whole port contract. Add a happy-path test verifying the returned HEAD and persisted file, plus an I/O failure case for the adapter mapping.

`Path::is_dir()` silently converts permission and other metadata failures into `false`, then reports every failure as a nonexistent track. This loses required adapter diagnostics and follows directory symlinks during the precheck. Use fallible metadata inspection, distinguish `NotFound`, explicitly reject symlinks, and propagate other I/O errors through sanitized `DiagnosticText`.

The new branch-mismatch and registry-fallback tests are not enrolled in the `resolve_views_scope` or `GitTrackSelectionAdapter` records in `test-bindings.json`; those records still cite only explicit success. Because the obligation references CN-01, the bound evidence still does not verify the preserved write guard or registry-only fallback. Bind these regression tests to the relevant obligations.

The new happy-path and symlink tests are not enrolled in the `TrackCommitHashPort` or `GitTrackCommitHashAdapter` records; both remain bound solely to the mismatch test that exits before HEAD resolution and persistence. Consequently the formal AC-05 contract evidence still does not cover the method's successful persistence behavior. Add the new tests to both binding records.

The branch-mismatch and registry-only fallback tests remain absent from both the `resolve_views_scope` fulfillment and `GitTrackSelectionAdapter` conformance records in `test-bindings.json`. The bound evidence still covers only successful resolution and therefore does not establish the CN-01 write guard or fallback behavior. Bind both regression tests to the relevant obligations.

The successful persistence, persistence-I/O failure, and symlink-rejection tests are not enrolled in the `TrackCommitHashPort` or `GitTrackCommitHashAdapter` records. Both obligations remain bound solely to the branch-mismatch test, which exits before HEAD resolution and persistence, so the formal AC-05 evidence still does not cover the adapter's core behavior. Add the new tests to both binding records.

Write/read resolution uses `SystemGitRepo::discover_from`, which honors ambient `GIT_DIR`; a caller can therefore resolve the branch from a different repository than the supplied workspace root, allowing the write guard to validate the wrong repository. Use the isolated discovery path for this gate-relevant adapter.

`InvalidTrackId` is converted to `Inactive`, silently treating a malformed `track/*` branch as “no active track.” This diverges from the existing fail-closed detection behavior, which only treats detached/no/non-track branches as inactive; malformed track branches should remain an unavailable/error outcome.

`discover_from_isolated` clears repository-selecting environment variables only during discovery. `ActiveTrackResolveInteractor` subsequently calls `SystemGitRepo::current_branch()`, which starts a new git process inheriting `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, and related variables. Consequently, `WriteFrom*` can validate an explicit track ID against a different repository's branch before callers write under the supplied workspace. Keep repository isolation in force for the branch read and add an environment-redirection regression test.

The adapter passes the caller-supplied workspace path directly to git without rejecting symlink components. For `WriteFromItems` and `WriteFromRoot`, the branch guard can therefore inspect a symlink target, and a retargeted link can make subsequent persistence operate on another tree. Apply the existing fail-closed real-file pattern (`reject_symlinks_up_to_root`/`discover_isolated_repo_for_items_dir`) before discovery and cover symlinked roots in tests, consistent with the symlink-rejection tests in `scope_config_loader.rs`.

The adapter reads `architecture-rules.json` before `BaselineCaptureInteractor` runs its root symlink guard. `TrackWorkspaceRoot` only rejects `..`, while `FsTdddLayerBindingsAdapter::load` assumes the supplied root is trusted; a symlinked workspace root is therefore followed before being rejected. Validate the trusted root before all preflight I/O, following the fail-closed trusted-root pattern.

The returned layer outcomes come from a pre-execution snapshot, while `run` reloads the bindings and independently checks each baseline. Concurrent replacement of `architecture-rules.json` or creation/deletion of a baseline can therefore return the wrong layer or report `Captured`/`AlreadyExists` contrary to what the operation did. The executing capture path must return the actual per-layer outcomes or operate from one guarded snapshot.

The selected `RustdocBaselineCaptureAdapter` writes CLI-formatted `[OK] baseline-capture ...` messages directly to stdout. Consequently this port is not presentation-free, despite returning structured layer results, and non-CLI callers receive unsolicited output. Keep the adapter stack silent and render outcomes in the primary adapter.

The tests only exercise the idempotent `AlreadyExists` success and a missing-config error. The primary missing-baseline path—which invokes rustdoc, writes the file, and returns `Captured`—has no test, leaving the new public adapter's main happy path unverified.

The result is synthesized from state observed before the actual capture. `run` reloads the bindings and the rustdoc adapter independently decides whether to write or skip each baseline. For example, two concurrent captures can both observe an absent file, then one invocation can skip the file written by the other while still returning `Captured`; concurrent deletion can similarly produce `AlreadyExists` after this invocation writes the file. Configuration replacement can also make the returned layer list differ from the layers actually processed. Return the actual per-layer outcomes from the executing capture path instead of reconstructing them from this preflight snapshot.

This wiring makes `TrackBaselineCapturePort::execute` invoke `RustdocBaselineCaptureAdapter`, whose success paths call `println!` with CLI-formatted `[OK] baseline-capture ...` messages. The port therefore has stdout presentation side effects even though it returns structured layer results, violating the briefing's presentation-free boundary. Make the capture adapter silent and render `TrackBaselineCaptureResult` in the primary adapter.

`bin/sotp test-obligation check --track-id 2026-08-15-track-lifecycle-pure-di` fails with unresolved edges: this file contains only 21 fulfillment records while `obligations.json` contains 101 obligations. Add fulfillment records for every derived obligation, or valid waivers where applicable, so the commit gate can establish totality.

The new TrackResolutionDriver × CN-01 voluntary binding at line 43 does not pass the deterministic obligation check: `bin/sotp test-obligation check --track-id 2026-08-15-track-lifecycle-pure-di` reports two `TestChanged` drifts because bound test bodies changed since their cached verdicts were frozen. Refresh/re-evaluate the obligation cache before accepting this binding.

The SystemTrackResolutionAdapter fulfillment binds only the ReadFromItems/Active happy-path test. Because this obligation covers both IN-04 and CN-01 without edge-specific waivers, that single assertion marks the entire adapter contract fulfilled while write guarding, inactive detection, and error behavior remain absent from the binding. Bind the existing write/detect/error tests and resolve CN-01 with appropriate edge-local evidence or a valid waiver.

The TrackResolutionDriver × IN-04 binding covers only Resolved and service-error outcomes. It omits the existing inactive-result and five-variant command-routing tests, so the central migrated driver behavior can pass the obligation gate without evidence for Inactive or four input-routing branches. Add those existing tests to this edge binding.

The SystemTrackResolutionAdapter fulfillment omits three current contract regressions: `test_system_track_resolution_adapter_write_guard_ignores_ambient_repository_selection`, `test_system_track_resolution_adapter_write_from_root_rejects_symlinked_workspace_root`, and `test_system_track_resolution_adapter_write_from_items_rejects_symlinked_items_path`. Consequently, the obligation gate does not protect the adapter’s repository-isolation and symlink-rejection behavior even though the adjacent waiver claims its write-guard and error behavior is bound by infrastructure tests. Add these tests to the fulfillment record.
CN-03 は「適切な command-context module」の判定基準を定義していないため、型設計・実装計画が配置の意味を独自に補う必要があり、観測可能な制約になっていません。

findings.category: goal not anchored to an ADR decision
findings.message: GO-01's “standalone reviewable and CI-green delivery unit” completion condition is unsupported by its cited decisions. The cited D4 covers CLI compatibility, D5 covers execution-path convergence, and realignment D1 covers wiring-only composition roots; none establishes track independence or CI-green integration. Those requirements appear in the initiative ADR's D2/D7, but GO-01 does not cite them, leaving part of the goal unanchored.
AC-07 は「canonical review results」や「他の未統合 migration track を必要とせず」の判定方法・成果物を特定しておらず、実装完了時に再現可能な deterministic check として観測できません。

findings.category: goal not anchored to an ADR decision
findings.message: GO-01 still includes “standalone reviewable and CI-green delivery unit” as part of the completion state, but none of its cited decisions supports that clause: initiative D4 covers external CLI compatibility, D5 covers removal of pure-DI deviations, and boundary-rules D1 covers wiring-only composition. The ADR passages mentioning standalone review/CI are D2/D7, which the current briefing explicitly classifies as non-binding implementation-procedure records that cannot ground later spec claims. This leaves part of the goal outside the cited decision space.

All per-command error types (e.g. `TrackAddTaskError`) include `InvalidCommand`, but every service accepts an already validated Command. The catalogue does not identify any path that can construct this variant, making the shared error surface structurally imprecise.

`TrackCommitHashPort`, `TrackMetadataPort`, and `TrackViewsPort` are synchronous despite declaring Git/filesystem I/O, while their docs do not acknowledge the synchronous choice. This leaves the port color contract ambiguous for adapters.

`TrackSelection` and `TrackViewsSyncScope` declare identical `Active`/`Explicit(domain::TrackId)` enums with the same role and invariants, but both are added independently rather than sharing one structural declaration or using a reference.

`cli_composition::TrackCompositionRoot.docs` and `cli_driver::TrackDriver.docs` restate upstream behavior contracts (wiring-only composition root; validate/invoke/render primary adapter) instead of describing the change plus anchor. See `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

The 15 command entries, including `usecase::TrackAddTaskCommand`, repeat the upstream validation/conversion contract (“Validated... all concept-bearing CLI inputs are converted before service execution”) in `docs`. This should be represented by the existing spec anchors, not duplicated prose. See `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

`usecase::TrackIdInput`, `usecase::TrackItemsDirectory`, and `usecase::TrackWorkspaceRoot` restate validation/enforcement behavior in `docs` instead of referencing the upstream contract by anchor. See `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

The command error entries, including `usecase::TrackAddTaskError`, repeat the presentation contract (“opaque diagnostic payloads for driver presentation”) in `docs`. This upstream behavior should remain in the spec and be referenced by anchor. See `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

`usecase::TrackResolveResult.docs` explains the design rationale that enum variants make blocker-only data structurally exclusive, restating an upstream type-shape contract. See `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

`cli_composition::TrackCompositionRoot` is a full-shape `modify` declaration but lists only `new` and `track_driver`. This implicitly removes the public methods defined in `track/tddd*.rs`, although `OUT-01` explicitly leaves those contexts untouched. The implementation cannot both match this catalogue and preserve the out-of-scope surface.

`cli_driver::TrackDriver::handle_set_commit_hash` requires `usecase::TrackIdInput`, which the production `cli` layer cannot depend on and which is not re-exposed through a driver-owned input. Conversely, `TrackTransitionCommand`, `TrackAddTaskCommand`, and `TrackSetOverrideCommand` require domain-only `TaskId`, `TaskTransition`, or `StatusOverrideKind` values but declare no usecase constructors or conversion functions. No legal delivery-layer caller can construct every validated command, leaving boundary validation without an owner.

`usecase::TrackBranchSwitchInteractor`, `TrackBranchCreateInteractor`, `TrackArchiveInteractor`, and `TrackSwitchBaseInteractor` inject `Arc<dyn GitWorkflowService>`, but the baseline trait has no branch-create, branch-switch, archive, workspace-scoped Git, or metadata-snapshot operations. No `modify` entry or replacement port supplies those capabilities, so these interactors cannot implement their declared execution paths from their collaborators.

`usecase::TrackInitInteractor` receives a preconstructed `BranchStrategyPort`, while the resolution interactors receive a preconstructed `ActiveTrackResolveService`; neither baseline contract accepts `TrackItemsDirectory` or `TrackWorkspaceRoot`. Since `TrackCompositionRoot::track_driver()` wires them before seeing command input, they cannot select the repository/config identified by `--items-dir` or `--project-root`, causing non-CWD invocations to resolve against the wrong workspace.

`usecase::TrackViewsSyncCommand.scope` uses `TrackSelection::{Active, Explicit}`, and `TrackViewsPort::sync` always requires a `TrackId`. The existing `TrackInput::ViewsSync` contract also supports registry-only synchronization when no active track exists, but the new command/port chain has no corresponding state. Synchronization on `main` or another non-track branch therefore cannot preserve the current behavior.

`usecase::TrackAddTaskResult` carries the new task's `TaskStatusKind` but drops the derived `TrackStatus` that the existing command prints as `track status`. The primary adapter cannot reconstruct that aggregate status from the command or task status without re-querying application state, so the declared result cannot preserve `CN-01` stdout.

`usecase::TrackResolveResult::Blocked` omits `phase` and provides only one `reason` field, while the lower-layer resolve output contains `phase`, `reason`, `next_command`, and a separate optional blocker; the current blocked-path stdout prints all four. The driver must therefore discard either the reason or blocker as well as the phase.

`cli_composition::TrackCompositionRoot` is a full-shape `modify`, but its method list omits `track_resolve_id`, `track_resolve_id_from_root`, `track_resolve_id_for_write`, and `track_resolve_id_from_root_for_write`. These APIs remain live in the out-of-scope ADR-baseline and review-v2 support contexts covered by OUT-02/OUT-03, so the declared post-shape either breaks surviving callers or requires undeclared public methods.

`usecase::TrackTransitionInteractor`, `TrackAddTaskInteractor`, `TrackSetOverrideInteractor`, and `TrackClearOverrideInteractor` inject the existing four-method `TaskOperationService`; the query interactors similarly retain `TaskQueryService`. The command-specific boundaries therefore still delegate through bundled application-service interfaces instead of directly depending on operation-specific ports, preserving the facade behind the new one-method services and forcing command-local implementations or mocks to provide unrelated methods.

`usecase::TrackBranchStrategyPort` and `usecase::TrackSelectionPort` are synchronous ports whose methods require filesystem/config and Git resolution, respectively, but their docs do not acknowledge the synchronous blocking-I/O choice. Their corresponding `FsTrackBranchStrategyAdapter` and `GitTrackSelectionAdapter` make the I/O color explicit, leaving the port contract ambiguous.

`TrackAddTaskResult`, `TrackTransitionResult::Transitioned`, `TrackSetOverrideResult`, and `TrackClearOverrideResult` represent view synchronization only as `Vec<RenderedViewPath>`. Existing behavior treats a post-persistence sync failure as command success with a diagnostic warning; an empty vector cannot distinguish that state from “already current,” while returning the diagnostic through the outer error would incorrectly change the exit status. The successful result path needs a typed warning/sync outcome.

`usecase::TrackArchiveResult.source` and `.destination` use `RenderedViewPath`, whose declared semantics are specifically a rendered-view path. Archive source and destination are track directories, so this reuse defeats the value object's semantic boundary and allows archive locations to be represented as rendered views; use an archive/directory path type instead.

`TrackResolutionCommand::DetectActive` can produce a valid inactive result, and `cli_driver::TrackResolutionOutcome` exposes `Inactive`, but `TrackResolutionService::execute` returns `Result<TrackResolutionResult, TrackResolutionCompatError>` where `TrackResolutionResult` always requires `track_id` and the only error is `Unavailable(DiagnosticText)`. The driver therefore cannot distinguish valid inactivity from failure while preserving diagnostics; one state must be lost.

`TrackResolutionCommand::DetectActive` can produce a valid inactive result, and `cli_driver::TrackResolutionOutcome` exposes `Inactive`, but `TrackResolutionService::execute` returns a `TrackResolutionResult` that always requires `track_id`, with only `Unavailable(DiagnosticText)` as an error. The driver cannot distinguish valid inactivity from failure while preserving diagnostics; one state must be lost.

`cli_driver::TrackDriver::new` still requires `legacy_track_service: Arc<dyn usecase::TrackService>`. This is the existing 16-operation bundled input port that the design requires dismantling; retaining a runtime dependency violates AC-04 and forces the driver to depend on operations already represented by narrow per-command services. OUT-03 permits unused compatibility definitions to remain, not active references. Remove this collaborator and route the remaining `TrackInput` variants through the narrow TDDD/resolution boundaries.

`cli_driver::TrackTdddInput` declares routes for only nine TDDD operations and omits the existing `TrackCompositionRoot::track_type_graph` execution method. No corresponding TypeGraph input, command, result, service, interactor, port, or adapter exists elsewhere in the scope. Because `TrackCompositionRoot`'s modified surface removes the original method, the required 34-method migration has no driver path that can preserve its current removed-command diagnostic.

The docs for `cli_driver::TrackItemsDirectoryInput`, `TrackLayerInput`, `TrackLayersInput`, `TrackLintRulesFileInput`, `TrackSourceWorkspaceInput`, `TrackSpecAnchorInput`, and `TrackWorkspaceRootInput` restate AC-03 behavior by specifying validation/parsing before boundary conversion. Under `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`, these entries must use a short identifying phrase and rely on `spec_refs` instead of reproducing that behavior contract.

The docs for `usecase::TrackBaselineCaptureLayerResult`, `TrackBaselineCaptureResult`, `TrackCatalogueSpecSignalsResult`, `TrackLayerSignalResult`, `TrackResolutionResult`, and `TrackTypeSignalsResult` explain their variant/field semantics and the rendering behavior guaranteed by AC-03/CN-01 or IN-04/CN-01. This reproduces upstream behavior and type-shape contracts rather than using anchor-backed identifying noun phrases, contrary to `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

`TrackTdddInput::TypeGraph` and `TrackTypeGraphService` expose a callable TypeGraph command, but `TrackTypeGraphResult` is an enum with zero variants and `TrackTypeGraphError` only has `RemovedCommand`. Consequently every advertised TypeGraph execution is unrepresentable as success and can only fail, leaving the driver/service contract incoherent.

`usecase::TaskQueryInteractor` is unconditionally declared to implement `TrackNextTaskQueryPort` and `TrackTaskCountsQueryPort`, whose commands allow `TrackSelection::Active`, but both `new(store)` and `with_branch_reader(store, None)` construct it without the collaborator required to resolve that variant. This makes a valid port implementation state unusable by construction. Require the resolver/reader for the new port implementation or move selection resolution exclusively into the command-specific interactors.

`usecase::TrackCatalogueLintActiveResult::Checked` flattens all layers into `Vec<CatalogueLintViolation>`, although `CatalogueLintViolation` contains no layer identity. The current command renders a `[layer]` prefix for every violation and reports the number of checked layers, so the primary adapter cannot reconstruct either part from this result. Preserve per-layer groups or include layer identity and the checked-layer count.

`usecase::TrackContractMapResult` omits the rendered-layer count, while the existing command's stdout includes `layers=<rendered_layer_count>` alongside the entry count and warnings. For `TrackLayerFilter::All`, that value cannot be derived by the primary adapter from the command, so CN-01 output equivalence is unrepresentable. Add `TrackRenderedLayerCount` to the result.
`TaskQueryInteractor` の `docs` が、型の識別名ではなく branch reader 注入と selection resolution の設計意図・挙動を再記述しています。`docs` は anchor cite と短い識別句に留めるべきです。
`TrackCatalogueLintLayerResult` の `docs` が、違反保持の挙動と primary adapter のレンダリング理由・checked-layer count を再記述しています。`.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md` に従い、anchor cite と短い識別句へ縮約すべきです。

`usecase::TaskQueryInteractor` still implements the baseline `TaskQueryService`, whose methods receive an explicit track ID, but its only post-change constructor now requires `BranchReaderPort`. This forces legacy explicit-ID query callers to inject an unused Git-selection collaborator and combines storage querying with active-track resolution, even though `TrackNextTaskInteractor` and `TrackTaskCountsInteractor` already inject `TrackSelectionPort`. Preserve the focused baseline constructor and move resolution solely to those command-specific interactors, or introduce a separate lifecycle adapter.

`TrackNextTaskQueryPort::next_task` and `TrackTaskCountsQueryPort::task_counts` accept an already validated `domain::TrackId` and perform no task mutation, yet return the nine-variant legacy `TaskOperationError`. Only query failures such as `TrackNotFound` and `StoreFailed` are reachable; `InvalidTrackId`, `InvalidTaskId`, `InvalidCommitHash`, `TaskNotFound`, `TransitionFailed`, `BranchGuardFailed`, and `BranchlessGuardFailed` cannot arise from these contracts. Introduce a query-specific error surface instead of forcing the narrow ports to expose unrelated variants.

The six command-specific secondary ports are declared in the shared `track_lifecycle` root instead of their approved command-context modules (`track_transition`, `track_add_task`, etc.). This leaves each per-subcommand module containing only its DTO and violates the 1-subcommand/1-usecase module boundary. Move each port beside its command/interactor, re-exporting it from the root if compatibility requires that path.

`test_task_interactors_implement_track_lifecycle_ports` only checks generic trait bounds; it never calls any of the six new public trait implementations or exercises explicit/active selection and failure propagation. Incorrect transition mapping, delegation, or branch-resolution behavior would still satisfy every recorded conformance binding. Add happy-path and error-path behavioral tests for these public APIs.

The new lifecycle tests import port traits from child command modules (for example `track_add_task::TrackTaskAddPort`), but those traits are defined/re-exported at `track_lifecycle` level and are not members of the child modules. The test target therefore fails to compile; import these traits from `crate::track_lifecycle::{...}` instead.

`TaskQueryInteractor` still owns `branch_reader` and resolves `TrackSelection::Active`, while the frozen contract requires query interactors to receive an already-resolved `domain::TrackId` and use `TrackSelectionPort` in command-specific interactors. The associated test calls the already-removed `TaskQueryInteractor::with_branch_reader` at line 960, so the usecase test target does not compile. Remove this query-side selection resolution and move Active-resolution tests to the later command-specific interactor tasks.

TaskOperationInteractor no longer implements the frozen secondary-port contracts. Those four ports must receive an already-resolved TrackId and validated domain arguments, but the new implementations accept Track*Command values containing TrackSelection and resolve Active through the legacy BranchReaderPort. This moves selection orchestration into the bundled legacy interactor and obstructs later one-usecase decomposition. Restore the catalogue signatures for transition/add/set/clear and remove this helper and its T001 Active-selection tests.

TrackNextTaskQueryPort returns TaskOperationError, while the frozen catalogue requires Result<Option<NextTaskOutput>, TrackNextTaskError>. Defining the trait with the legacy shared error means TaskQueryInteractor only conforms to the altered local trait, not the frozen usecase contract.

TrackTaskCountsQueryPort returns TaskOperationError, while the frozen catalogue requires Result<TaskCountsOutput, TrackTaskCountsError>. This changes the usecase error boundary and prevents TaskQueryInteractor from implementing the declared frozen contract.

`TaskOperationInteractor`'s four new secondary-port implementations (`TrackTaskTransitionPort`, `TrackTaskAddPort`, `TrackOverrideSetPort`, and `TrackOverrideClearPort`) accept command-context objects and resolve `TrackSelection` themselves. The frozen catalogue requires these ports to receive an already-resolved `domain::TrackId` plus typed operation arguments; selection belongs in the later command-specific interactors through `TrackSelectionPort`. This also makes the T001 Active-failure test at `task_ops.rs:973` cement behavior assigned to later decomposition. Align all four traits/impls with the catalogued signatures and remove the added selection resolver and misplaced test.

`TrackNextTaskQueryPort` returns the broad `TaskOperationError`, while the frozen contract requires `TrackNextTaskError`; `TrackTaskCountsQueryPort` has the analogous mismatch with `TrackTaskCountsError` at `track_task_counts.rs:22`. Their implementations therefore expose mutation and branch-guard failures that cannot arise from these storage queries and leave T007/T014 requiring a breaking interface change. Use and map the command-specific query error types.
